text:
North East founders: you have until 5 December to get into a MeitY-backed accelerator whose last cohort gave each startup ₹10 lakh in grants.

Digi-SAPNE 3.0 is the third edition of the North East Startup Acceleration Programme, run by AIC-SMU Technology Business Incubation Foundation at Sikkim Manipal University with funding support from MeitY. The official page puts the grant pool at up to ₹80 lakh, and in the previous cohort that worked out to ₹10 lakh for each selected startup.

Beyond the money, selected teams go through a growth-hack programme to sharpen strategy, a market-access track, mentoring and workshops, and finish with an investors' meet and demo day.

It is open to early-stage, tech-enabled startups from the eight North Eastern states: Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura. This edition gives priority to tourism, agritech and AI, ventures with some early traction are preferred, and registering as a Private Limited company is advised.

The catch: the official page does not state a closing time, so treat 4 December night as your real deadline rather than risking the last day.

Last date: 5 December 2026

text:
Did you know NABARD runs a fund that can put up to ₹25 crore of equity into a single agri or rural startup, and you apply with an email?

The AgriSURE Direct Scheme is managed by NABVENTURES, NABARD's investment arm. AgriSURE itself is a ₹750 crore SEBI-registered Category II AIF backed by the Government of India and NABARD, and its direct scheme invests equity or equity-linked instruments such as CCPS straight into companies, released in tranches with the possibility of follow-on money in later rounds.

It suits DPIIT-recognised startups incorporated in India working in agriculture, allied and rural sectors: agritech, food processing, animal husbandry, fisheries, supply chain, farm mechanisation or renewable energy. You need to be past the idea and prototype stage, with a steady revenue stream and a differentiated business model.

Proposals are taken on a rolling basis: send your pitch deck or company profile to agrisure@nabard.org. There is no application fee, and NABARD warns against agents who ask for money to get you in.

The tip founders miss: this is VC-style money, so expect dilution and full due diligence. If you are still pre-revenue, AgriSURE-backed sector funds or RKVY-RAFTAAR incubators are usually a better first stop.

text:
Building a startup in Uttarakhand? The state will give you up to ₹10 lakh in seed money, and up to ₹12.5 lakh if you are a woman, SC/ST, divyang or rural founder, without taking any equity.

The Seed Fund under the Uttarakhand Startup Policy 2023 is run by the Startup Cell of the state's Department of Industries. It is one-time support to help a recognised startup take its product to market, and disruptive-technology ventures can get an extra ₹2.5 lakh on top.

To qualify, you need recognition under the Uttarakhand Startup Policy, a company, LLP or registered partnership registered in or operating from Uttarakhand, an entity under 10 years old, and turnover below ₹100 crore. The Startup Council selects startups on the merit of the innovation.

The process is simple on paper: sign up on the Startup Uttarakhand portal, get your state Certificate of Recognition, then use "Apply for Incentives" on your dashboard. Keep your pitch deck or business plan and incorporation certificate ready.

One thing to plan for: the money is released on Startup Council approval and typically in tranches, so do not budget as if the full amount lands on day one.
